newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sappi 12-week Adamas mill strike resolved.
newsitem.headline: Sappi 12-week Adamas mill strike resolved.

text.p: South African paper producer Sappi Ltd said on Monday the 12-week wage strike at its Adamas mill in the Eastern Cape city of Port Elizabeth had been resolved.
"The agreement signed today gives the Adamas workers a 7.5 percent increase in basic wages plus a 175 rand signing bonus," Sappi said in a statement.
It said the deal was effective until April 23 1998.
The 167 members of the Congress of South African Trade Unions aligned Paper, Printing, Wood and Allied Workers' Union (PPWAWU) had agreed to return to work on July 15.
Sappi said the mill was the only one within the group where wage negotiations were protracted and the dispute had to go to mediation.
PPWAWU members at some of the group's other operations embarked on a 24-hour sympathy strike on July 7.
Production at the Adamas mill was not affected and regular supplies to customers were maintained throughout the 12 week strike, Sappi said.
